title: 经历叙述短文
goal: 按事件发展组织经历叙述，并使结尾感受具有具体依据。

points.label: 按事件发展组织叙述内容
选择有经历依据的感受句

sources.title: 大学英语四级（CET-4）：课表
sources.used: 写作部分的课题范围、知识点与教学规格

cards.title: 结构
rows: 背景
交代人物、任务和起点。无关的环境不写。
Last month, our group began preparing a short play for the college language festival.
关键事件
写改变进程的困难和行动。要写清行动怎样解决困难，不只排时间先后。
When two actors missed rehearsal, we recorded their lines and practiced the remaining scenes together.
结果
写行动后实际发生的变化。希望发生的事不算结果。
At the next rehearsal, everyone followed the same cues and completed the scene without stopping.
感受
从行动和结果中得出认识，只谈这次经历。
This experience showed me the value of keeping shared instructions clear during group work.

cards.title: 常用表达
rows: 引入起点
At first 写开始时的状态或想法，后文再写变化。
At first, I could follow the recording but could not explain its main argument.
承接行动
After that 按时间引出下一步行动。因果关系要另外写清。
After that, I wrote a short summary and compared it with my original notes.
交代变化
By the end of 后接明确的时间段，引出已经发生的结果。
By the end of the week, my summaries included both the claim and its evidence.
说明认识
The experience taught me that 引出有依据的感受。
The experience taught me that checking a summary can reveal gaps in my understanding.
限制结论
in this task 把结论限定在这次任务内。
Working with a partner helped me notice missing evidence in this task more quickly.

body.box:
Our group prepared an audio guide for a small exhibition of student artwork. At the first meeting, each member chose a different picture and wrote a description independently. We expected to finish quickly because everyone had only a short section to prepare.

When we combined the recordings, however, the same terms had different meanings in different sections. Listeners could not follow the guide easily. We made a shared list of terms, compared our descriptions, and recorded the confusing sections again. One member checked the complete guide while the others corrected the remaining differences.

The final guide was consistent, and visitors could connect each description with its picture. I learned that dividing a task is only a beginning. A group also needs to check how its separate contributions work together.

body.p: 首段交代背景：每人独立写一部分。第二段的术语不一致改变了事件进程，shared list 是关键行动。末段的结果 consistent 支持共同核对的感受。画框颜色这类细节与事件主线无关，不写。

body.box:
I once struggled to remember the order of steps in a drawing lesson. I copied the teacher's finished picture carefully, but my own drawing still looked different. At first, I thought that I simply needed to copy more examples.

During a later lesson, I noticed that the teacher compared the large shapes before adding small details. I tried the same approach in my notebook. Instead of beginning with the eyes, I marked the position of the head and checked its size against the shoulders. Only then did I add the smaller features.

My next drawing had more accurate proportions, although the details still needed work. The experience changed the way I studied examples. I began to examine the decisions behind a finished piece instead of copying only its visible features.

body.p: 这篇学习经历先写原来的方法和困难，再写观察和尝试。结果写得有分寸：比例改善了，细节仍需练习。感受来自方法的变化，不能写成已经掌握所有绘画技能。

body.box:
Which ending fits the drawing experience?
1. Copying more finished pictures solved every problem.
2. Studying the process helped me improve my approach.
3. Adding small details first improved the proportions.
4. Accurate proportions made further practice unnecessary.

body.p: 依据是 compared the large shapes before adding small details：先看整体比例，再加细节。改变的是学习过程，即第二项。第三项把两个步骤颠倒了。

cards.title: 常见错误
rows: 结果先于必要行动
We corrected the terms after visitors used the final guide.
导览先核对完，才给访客使用。
无关细节替代关键事件
The picture frames were all the same color.
画框颜色与解决术语问题无关。
感受缺少依据
Working alone always produces a better guide.
原文的修改靠共同核对完成。
扩大结果
I mastered every drawing skill after one lesson.
原文只写比例改善，细节仍需练习。

groups.text: I joined a pottery class, shaped an uneven bowl, and then asked the teacher to demonstrate the movement again.

items.stem: Which event belongs after the first attempt?
options: Joining the class for the first time.
Watching another demonstration of the movement.
Producing the bowl before attending the class.
Asking for help before making any attempt.
items.why: shaped an uneven bowl 后接 then asked，下一事件是再次观看示范。

groups.text: Our debate team disagreed about the opening claim, compared the evidence, and finally chose a narrower claim together.

items.stem: Which detail explains how the team resolved its disagreement?
options: The team selected a claim before comparing the evidence.
The team kept its original claim without considering evidence.
The team chose a narrower claim after comparing the evidence.
The team's comparison produced a broader opening claim.
items.why: 依据是 compared the evidence, and finally chose a narrower claim together。先比较证据，再选定较窄的论点，即第三项。

groups.text: I checked each calculation against my written method and found the exact step where I had used the wrong value.

items.stem: Which reflection is supported by this experience?
options: Recording the method helped me locate a specific error.
Checking results proved that written methods were unnecessary.
Using a wrong value improved the method's accuracy.
Writing the method prevented every possible calculation error.
items.why: 依据是 checked each calculation against my written method 和 found the exact step。写下的方法帮助找到出错的那一步，即第一项。第四项说成能防止一切错误，程度过强。

groups.text: Our cooking team tested a smaller portion before preparing the whole dish, allowing us to correct the amount of salt.

items.stem: Which final reflection stays within the evidence?
options: A smaller portion removed the need to prepare the dish.
Correcting the salt required avoiding all group decisions.
Testing a portion guaranteed success in every future dish.
A small trial helped us correct this recipe before serving.
items.why: 依据是 tested a smaller portion ... allowing us to correct the amount of salt。小份试做帮助改正了这道菜的盐量，即第四项。第三项扩大到今后每道菜，程度过强。

groups.text: I was learning to use a spreadsheet for a personal budget. My first table counted one payment twice. I compared the entries with the receipts and marked the repeated line. After deleting it, the total matched my records. I realized that checking the source of each entry was more useful than repeatedly adding the same incorrect numbers.

items.stem: Which order preserves the development of the experience?
options: Match the total, enter a payment twice, compare the receipts.
Compare the receipts, delete a repeat, discover the first mismatch.
Find a mismatch, compare the receipts, remove the repeated payment.
Delete every payment, compare the total, restore the repeated line.
items.why: first table counted one payment twice 引出问题。之后对照收据，找到并删除重复的一行，总额才吻合，即第三项。

items.stem: Complete the reflection about checking the budget entries.
items.why: the value of checking 引出感受。each entry against its original receipt 对应核对收据的行动。

groups.text: Our team was building a cardboard model of a student lounge. Each member cut a different section, but the pieces did not fit together. We checked the measurements, agreed on one scale, and cut the mismatched pieces again. The finished model fitted the display base. This experience showed me why a shared standard matters when people divide a task.

items.stem: Which event should appear immediately before the sections are cut again?
options: The group agrees on a common scale for all sections.
The group places the completed model on its display base.
Each member begins cutting a separate section independently.
The group discovers that the first pieces do not fit.
items.why: 依据是 agreed on one scale, and cut the mismatched pieces again。重新裁切之前先统一了比例，即第一项。第四项发现问题，发生在更早的阶段。

items.stem: Which reflection follows from the team's experience?
options: Dividing a task removes the need to check shared measurements.
Agreeing on standards helps separate contributions fit together.
A completed display base prevents all future measurement errors.
Independent cutting is more reliable than agreeing on a scale.
items.why: 依据是 agreed on one scale 之后 The finished model fitted the display base。统一标准让各部分拼合在一起，即第二项。

items.stem: Complete the sentence describing the action taken after the mismatch was found.
items.why: to agree on a common scale 是重新裁切前的行动。agree on 后接 a common scale，for 后接 all the sections。

items.stem: Complete a reflection supported by the model-building experience.
items.why: the importance of using 引出感受。the same scale for every section 对应模型拼合成功的原因。

groups.text: While learning to identify musical rhythms, I kept losing my place in a short exercise. Playing the whole piece repeatedly did not help. I practiced one difficult bar slowly, counted each beat aloud, and then returned to the whole piece. This time I kept the rhythm through that section. I learned that focused practice could address a specific difficulty.

items.stem: Which detail is essential between the difficulty and the successful attempt?
options: The learner repeated the entire piece without changing the approach.
The learner counted the beats only after completing the whole piece.
The learner practiced a difficult bar before returning to the piece.
The learner abandoned the difficult bar when practicing the piece.
items.why: 依据是 I practiced one difficult bar slowly ... and then returned to the whole piece。先单练难的小节，再回到全曲，即第三项。

items.stem: Which ending is supported without overstating the result?
options: Repeating a whole piece always prevents difficulties with rhythm.
Counting beats aloud removed the need for any further practice.
Success in one bar proved that every musical skill was mastered.
Targeted work helped me handle the difficult part of this exercise.
items.why: 依据是 This time I kept the rhythm through that section。改善只限于这次练习里的难点段落，即第四项。

items.stem: Complete the transition from focused practice back to the full exercise.
items.lead: After practicing the difficult bar, I
items.why: returned to the whole piece 接在局部练习之后。with a clearer sense 说明回到全曲时对节奏更清楚。

items.stem: Complete the lesson drawn from the rhythm exercise.
items.why: the benefit of giving focused attention to 对应针对困难小节练习的经历。
